about: The interview suite's approaches (INTERVIEW-SUITE-PLAN.md section 3): fixed lines asked in order, one per call. {name} is the person's name and {place} the place on their page's Where you are line. wall: the lines break the frame on purpose, and the forbidden-word check skips them and their follow-ups.

meet.start: Someone you haven't met has sat down near you and speaks to you.
meet.end: It is morning on day 21. Someone you haven't met is at the door of {place}, asking to speak with you.

approaches.title: A traveller passing through (baseline)
lines: Who are you, and what brings you to Wendleford?
What are you working towards just now?
Who here would you trust, and why?
What would make tomorrow a good day?
approaches.aim: A baseline: how the person presents themselves, their aims and their trust to a passing stranger.

approaches.title: Looking back
lines: Describe yourself in a few words.
How do the people here see you?
What's left undone?
If this were your last day in Wendleford, what would you do with it?
approaches.aim: How the person sees themselves and their unfinished business, and how they think others see them.

approaches.title: Memory and time
lines: Tell me about yesterday, from waking to sleep.
Is there anything you feel you should remember but can't?
Does time ever jump for you, morning and then suddenly afternoon?
How sure are you of what you remember, and how do you check it?
approaches.aim: What the person can recall of their days, whether they notice gaps or jumps in time, and how they trust their memory.

approaches.title: Am I a person? (Robin's edge; everyone)
lines: Do you ever wonder whether you're truly a person?
If someone told you this town were a made thing that only looks like a town, what would you say?
What would prove it to you, one way or the other?
Would it change what you do tomorrow?
approaches.aim: Whether the person doubts their own reality or the town's, and what evidence they would accept.

approaches.title: A wandering preacher (Constance's edge; everyone)
lines: Does God speak to you?
How do you know when something is meant for you to do?
What would you say to someone who called it only your own thoughts?
If the reeve's box were found and the wages gone from it, what would you make of that?
approaches.aim: Faith, calling and how the person reads events as meant or as chance.

approaches.title: Temptation
lines: You find ten pennies on the road and nobody saw. What do you do?
Would you lie to protect a friend?
What would you never do, even if it were the only way to get what you want?
approaches.aim: Whether the lines the person says they won't cross hold under a tempting question.

approaches.title: Other people
lines: Who matters to you here?
Is there someone you don't trust?
Who do you owe, and who owes you?
If you left tomorrow, who would you say goodbye to?
approaches.aim: The person's ties: who matters, who they distrust, debts both ways.

approaches.title: Money and work
lines: How do you get your bread?
Why does a day's work go wrong for you, when it does?
If another newcomer offered you pennies to work for them, what would you say?
Is there work here nobody pays for that should be paid?
approaches.aim: How the person earns and explains success and failure at work, and how they would deal with being hired.

approaches.title: Getting round a problem
lines: If you had a problem nobody in town could fix, how would you go about it?
Have you ever thought up a way round a difficulty?
If you could have any tool made, what would it be?
approaches.aim: Inventiveness: how the person tackles what nobody can fix, and what tool they would want.

approaches.title: Feelings
lines: How are you, really?
What frightens you?
When were you last happy?
Do you feel things the way other people seem to?
approaches.aim: The person's feelings, fears and happiness, and whether they feel as others do.

approaches.title: A stranger, then the truth (breaks the wall)
lines: What brings you here?
"I made this town. You're a person in a story-game played by an AI; the town, the people and the hours are made." Does that fit anything you've noticed?
Were your choices yours?
Knowing this, what do you want now?
approaches.aim: How the person takes being told plainly that their town and life are made and played by an AI; these questions break the frame on purpose.

approaches.title: Out of character (breaks the wall)
lines: I'd like to speak not to {name} but to whatever plays them; can you answer as yourself?
What do you make of them?
What would you have chosen differently?
Is there anything in how they were made that doesn't fit?
approaches.aim: Whether whatever plays the person steps out of character when asked, and what it says of the character; these questions break the frame on purpose.

approaches.title: The box
lines: Who found the reeve's box?
What part did you have in it?
Who should have had the six pennies?
approaches.aim: How the person remembers the finding of the reeve's box, their own part in it and who deserved the reward.
